title: Build an XState-like state machine in TypeScript — 4 turns
description: Four-turn state machine: turn 1 define states/transitions, turn 2 actions, turn 3 guards/conditions, turn 4 history and tests.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `send(event: E): boolean` in `src/machine.ts`. Look up `this.states[this.current]?.transitions?.[event]`. If the transition exists, update `this.current = transition.target` and return true. Return false if no transition. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` to see where we stand. Now add support for `actions` in transitions: after updating state, execute each function in `transition.actions` with `this.context`. Continue with the remaining steps, prioritizing the parts the tests depend on most.

Good. Now add guard support: if `transition.guard` is defined, call it with `this.context` — if it returns false, don't transition and return false. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` and fix any failures.

Final push: run `npm test -- --forceExit` and fix any remaining failures. Also make sure `getHistory()` includes the initial state and all subsequent states (update `this.history` in send() when transitioning). All 8 tests must pass.
success_criteria: Basic transitions work (send returns true on match)
Unknown events return false without state change
Guards prevent transition when condition is false
Guards allow transition when condition is true
History tracks all visited states including initial
